l.i: DEfinite ô tandem : quid enim indulgetis inani
Ac primum tibi Mars, primum tibi Pallas
Imò agite, & Diuæ (sic fas expostulat) vni
Definite ô: quid enim studia in contraria vates
Imò agite, & Diuam sociatis laudibus vnam
Artibus Aoniis vincit quæ Pallada, vincit
Illa suos longa, quàm longa, pace Britannos,
Nec dum alius bello, tot iam labentibus annis,
Aggressi innumera vix tandem classe Gigantis
Mentior? anne ipso dirimi hæc certamina vultis

page.notes: The first word of the poem is a large woodcut-style initial "D" followed by "efinite"; transcribed as "Definite" with the initial joined. The first line's "Defi-nite" is read as "Definite" after the initial, with "Essinite" in the scan. Words with a long-s form were normalised to plain s. Uncertain readings: "Definite" (first line) and "Liuore" (appears clearly). No illegible words. Ornamented catchword/signature absent.
